name: Robert Cameron Rogers
bio: Robert Cameron Rogers (1862–1912) was an American poet, born at Buffalo, New York, who died at Santa Barbara, California, in 1912.
He is remembered chiefly for his song-lyric “The Rosary”, which was set to music by Ethelbert Nevin and became one of the most popular parlour songs of its time.

poems.title: The Rosary
poems.author: Robert Cameron Rogers
poems.collection: The Little Book of Modern Verse (1913)
poems.text:
The hours I spent with thee, dear heart,
 Are as a string of pearls to me;
I count them over, every one apart,
        My rosary.

Each hour a pearl, each pearl a prayer,
 To still a heart in absence wrung;
I tell each bead unto the end -- and there
        A cross is hung.

Oh, memories that bless -- and burn!
 Oh, barren gain -- and bitter loss!
I kiss each bead, and strive at last to learn
        To kiss the cross,
         Sweetheart,
        To kiss the cross.
